note: Owner anchors 2026-11-11: a regular looking roughly the right way spots a man standing still in the open at 300 m in about 5-15 s (base rate 0.07 per s: median 10 s); a man lying still in crops at 100 m is very hard to spot until he moves or fires. Chance per scan = 1 - exp(-rate x scan time); rate = base x (reference range / range)^2 x exposed size by posture x movement or firing x visibility along the line of sight x where he is looking x optic x skill x stress x light. Moving through vegetation shows at least 15 % of a man (plants move); firing at least 50 % (flash, dust). A man already seen is kept with 200 times the rate (once seen, easy to keep) and forgotten after 6 s unseen. All game values for review in the spotting lab. A man keeps track of at most 6 enemies at a time (the nearest); others he has seen pass into what his side knows (contacts, M3.3). Sensors (review fix): every man has his eyes; a weapon sight adds its kind, an item with a `sensor` (night-vision goggle) adds that; the best applies: factor beyond `fromM`, and light counts as at least `nightLight` (night vision, thermal). Moving or firing inside vegetation: the plants or the flash above him show if the line to the top of the vegetation over him is clear (not through a wood). Contacts (M3.3): seen positions are exact to 1 m + 1 % of range; a shot heard within 1,500 m gives the direction (8 degrees error) and a distance guess (35 % error) — owner: direction at once, position only if seen; a contact is forgotten after 2 minutes, its uncertainty grows 1 m per second of age; a man passes on what he sees or hears to his unit every 10 s at most — by voice within the comms model's voice range after 1 s, by radio after the comms model's delay; a reported position is 5 m less certain; a unit calls out new contacts on the radio at most every 8 s. Smoke (M6.5c): the view through smoke falls by exp(-0.15 per metre): 15 m of smoke leaves about a tenth, a 50 m screen nothing (game value).
